title: Is it possible that that player Shakespeare, a ghost by absence, and in the vesture of buried Denmark, a ghost by death, speaking his own words to his own son’s name (had Hamnet Shakespeare lived he would have been prince Hamlet’s twin), is it possible, I want to know, or probable that he did not draw or foresee the logical conclusion of those premises: you are the dispossessed son: I am the murdered father: your mother is the guilty queen, Ann Shakespeare, born Hathaway?
html_source:
A biographical interpretation of Hamlet by Stephen. He’s asking the others to consider that as Shakespeare was playing Hamlet’s ghost, it would have sparked remorse at the death of his son. In other words the writing of Hamlet isn’t to illuminate the unseen world AE refers to but is rooted in the real world of the writer.

dispossessed son – Hamnet Shakespeare
the murdered father – Shakespeare
the guilty queen – Ann Hathaway
